# Introduction

Factors such as crop yield, income and health outcomes can be heavily influenced by geography. This activity will serve as an introduction to including neighbors as predictors in an Ordinary Least Squares(OLS) model. 

## Load necessary packages

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf) # package to use spatial features in R
library(tigris) # package with county boundaries
library(spdep) # package to create neighborhoods
library(spatialreg) # package to spatially model data
```

# 1. Mapping Review

Use the given data to create a map of both the soybean production by county in Minnesota, as well as the average precipitation by county.

```{r}
# Using `USAboundaries` read in the shapefiles for states
countiesMN <- counties(state = "MN")

crops <- read_csv("../data/clean/crop_production.csv") |> 
  filter(stateID == 27) |> 
  select(COUNTYFP = countyID, soybean)

precip <- read_csv("../data/clean/climate_county.csv") |> 
  filter(state == "Minnesota") |> 
  select(COUNTYFP = ID3, precip = precip2125)

joined_counties <- countiesMN |> 
  left_join(crops, by = join_by(COUNTYFP)) |> 
  left_join(precip, by = join_by(COUNTYFP))

joined_counties |> 
  ggplot(aes(fill = precip)) +
  geom_sf()
```

# 2. Methods for analyzing neighbors

## Rook and Queen Neighbors

This will assign neighbors based if the two regions share a point(Queen) or share a border(Rook). Comment on the difference(or lack thereof!) between the two neighborhood structures.

```{r}
queen_nb <- poly2nb(countiesMN, queen = TRUE)
rook_nb <- poly2nb(countiesMN, queen = FALSE) #Does rook structure

queen_lines <- nb2lines(nb = queen_nb, coords = centroids, as_sf = TRUE)
rook_lines <- nb2lines(nb = rook_nb, coords = centroids, as_sf = TRUE)

a <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = countiesMN) +
  geom_sf(data = queen_lines) +
  labs(title = "Queen Neighborhood Structure") +
  ggthemes::theme_map()

b <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = countiesMN) +
  geom_sf(data = rook_lines) +
  labs(title = "Rook Neighborhood Structure") +
  ggthemes::theme_map()

library(patchwork)
a+b
```


## K-Nearest Neighbors

Each region will be given at minimum K neighbors. Choose a reasonable number of neighbors to give each region. Then plot the neighbors and weigh pros and cons.

```{r}
centroids <- st_centroid(st_geometry(countiesMN), of_largest_polygon = TRUE)

knn_nb <- knn2nb(knearneigh(centroids, k = ???))

knn_lines <- nb2lines(nb = knn_nb, coords = centroids, as_sf = TRUE)

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = countiesMN) +
  geom_sf(data = knn_lines) +
  labs(title = "KNN Neighborhood Structure") +
  ggthemes::theme_map()
```

## Distance-Based Neighbors

Neighbors will be assigned if they fall within a given distance range. Choose a distance, in kilometers to which you want to consider two counties neighbors.

```{r}
dist_nb <- dnearneigh(centroids, d1 = 0, d2 = ???) # km if geographical coordinates

dist_lines <- nb2lines(nb = distnb, coords = centroids, as_sf = TRUE)

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = countiesMN) +
  geom_sf(data = dist_lines)
```
